purpose: Ranked, nonredundant embodied sky-orientation factoids for Oracle of Relphi. Rank 1 is most worthy to share.
ranking_policy: Prioritize usable embodied conversions, surprising insight, factual reliability, and novelty. Compare new entries with existing ones before adding; avoid duplicate principles and near-identical variations. Re-rank after every addition.

factoids.title: A ruler becomes a celestial protractor
factoids.fact: Hold a ruler about 57.3 cm (22.6 in) from your eye: 1 cm spans approximately 1° of sky, and 1 mm spans about 6 arcminutes.
factoids.application: Use a measured physical length to feel the scale of chart angles; 5 mm is approximately the apparent width of the Moon.
factoids.caveat: Hold the ruler perpendicular to the line of sight; this measures apparent angular separation, not necessarily ecliptic-longitude differences.
